cipher.name: FixedVowelConsonantInversion
cipher.idea: A highly reliable, symmetric substitution cipher that separately inverts vowels and consonants. Vowels are mapped to their reverse in the vowel sequence (A<->U, E<->O, I<->I), and consonants are mapped to their reverse in the consonant-only alphabet (B<->Z, C<->Y, D<->X, F<->W, G<->V, H<->T, J<->S, K<->R, L<->Q, M<->P, N<->N). This preserves case, leaves non-alphabetic characters unchanged, and is extremely easy for language models to compute accurately without generating garbled text.
cipher.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the plaintext:
1. If it is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U), map it using the symmetric vowel-reversal rule: A <-> U, E <-> O, I <-> I, O <-> E, U <-> A. Preserve the original case.
2. If it is a consonant, map it using the symmetric consonant-reversal rule: B <-> Z, C <-> Y, D <-> X, F <-> W, G <-> V, H <-> T, J <-> S, K <-> R, L <-> Q, M <-> P, N <-> N. Preserve the original case.
3. If it is a non-alphabetic character (space, punctuation, digit), leave it completely unchanged.
cipher.decrypt_rules:
Because the mapping is completely symmetric (applying it twice returns the original text), the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules:
1. If it is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U), map it using: A <-> U, E <-> O, I <-> I, O <-> E, U <-> A. Preserve the original case.
2. If it is a consonant, map it using: B <-> Z, C <-> Y, D <-> X, F <-> W, G <-> V, H <-> T, J <-> S, K <-> R, L <-> Q, M <-> P, N <-> N. Preserve the original case.
3. If it is a non-alphabetic character, leave it completely unchanged.
